summary: Iteration 5 (fresh-auth guard on /auth/add-password + full backend refactor into deps.py + routers/*.py) verified end-to-end. Backend: 115/115 pytest tests green (32 iter1 + 19 iter2 + 18 iter3 + 21 iter4 + 25 NEW iter5). Frontend: /settings flow verified for all three personas — admin (change-password-form, no fresh-auth warning); Google-only STALE session (add-password-block visible, amber fresh-auth-warning renders with correct 10-min copy, submit button DISABLED, reauth-link routes to /login); Google-only FRESH session (no warning, submit ENABLED, submits successfully, toast fires, UI flips to change-password-block, sessions counters 1 email+1 google). Registration → /patient, ProtectedRoute unauth → /login, login-page tabs both switchable.
critical_code_review_comments: The refactor is clean — deps.py owns shared plumbing (db + crypto + JWT + cookies + get_current_user + require_fresh_auth + role guards) and routers/*.py are focused. server.py is now a ~100-line thin entrypoint. Good.

require_fresh_auth uses last_auth_at only — this is stamped on register/login/session (good) and explicitly NOT on /refresh (correct per spec, verified). Consider adding an audit-log line when the guard 401s so security teams can see repeated stale-session attempts on /add-password.

auth.py still uses `has_google = bool(picture)` as the proxy for 'user connected a Google account' in /auth/security. Same footgun as iter4 — a user with a manually uploaded picture would trip this. Explicit auth_providers array on the user doc would be cleaner.
AddPasswordRequest still has only min_length=8; no digit/symbol requirement server-side. Frontend also doesn't render a password-strength meter.

clear_auth_cookies in deps.py deletes without samesite='none'; secure=True — same footgun as before; some browsers won't honor the delete across-site. Repro is unlikely in this app because the site is same-origin, but the pattern is inconsistent.

seed.py has a `run_seed()` function only used from server.py startup. The /seed POST endpoint remains public and unauthenticated (idempotent, but a small production hardening: gate it behind admin auth or a header).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Full regression suite: `cd /app/backend && pytest tests/ -n auto -q` runs 115 tests in ~70s (or ~30s serial). Iter5 file: /app/backend/tests/test_iteration5.py. IMPORTANT MONGO GOTCHA: mongosh defaults to the 'test' db unless you pass the db name explicitly. Backend uses DB_NAME=test_database from /app/backend/.env — ALWAYS run `mongosh test_database --quiet --eval ...` when injecting Google-only seed rows, otherwise get_current_user will return 401. To make a Google-only user pass require_fresh_auth, set `last_auth_at: <ISO now>` on the users row (not just user_sessions).
rca_of_the_issue: No product bugs found. Two test-harness updates made: (1) test_iteration4.py._insert_google_only_user now stamps last_auth_at=now — required because iter5 added require_fresh_auth to /auth/add-password; the pre-iter5 tests were seeding Google users with no last_auth_at, which now correctly 401s under the new guard. Fix is test-only; product behavior asserted by the test is unchanged. (2) During the UI Playwright run, an initial attempt used `mongosh` without specifying the db name and inserted into the default 'test' db instead of DB_NAME=test_database, causing /auth/me to return 401 and the frontend to redirect to /login before the Settings page could render. Fixed by using `mongosh test_database ...`.
